page: Amazon Web Services is4gen.xlarge is an Arm-based storage-optimized virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It provides 4 dedicated physical cores (4 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading) running AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem is backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware acceleration for AES encryption. Memory capacity sits at 24.0 GB of RAM, offering a 1:6 vCPU-to-memory ratio (6.0 GB per core). For high-throughput local I/O, the instance bundles 3,750 GB of dedicated local NVMe SSD storage, accompanied by a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. No discrete GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark evaluations show a platform structured around high-capacity local storage rather than compute intensity. While single-core stress-ng tests hit the middle 50% tier at 1,519.48, overall multi-core computational scores, including Geekbench multi-core (3,226.0) and PassMark CPU (2,699.24), fall within the bottom 25% and 10% tiers respectively. Vector processing lacks AVX or AMX extensions, leading to modest small-model LLM inference throughput of 26.69 tokens per second for text generation. However, large-block memory bandwidth remains stable in the middle 50% tier at 73.07 GB/sec read and 35.12 GB/sec write, while PassMark database operations also maintain average tier results at 2,615.53.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, is4gen.xlarge pairs power-efficient Arm architecture with exceptionally high NVMe capacity per vCPU, avoiding the overhead of larger compute allocations when raw processing power is secondary to local storage density. This profile is suited for distributed data stores, intermediate data warehousing nodes, log analytics clusters, and local database caching engines where massive fast NVMe storage and balanced memory outweigh raw compute demand.
description: Amazon Web Services is4gen.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System, utilizing a 4-core AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. It integrates 24.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:6 vCPU-to-memory allocation, and features 3,750 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 6 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance omits GPU acceleration. Synthetic benchmarks reflect conservative CPU performance, with multi-core Geekbench and PassMark CPU tests placing in the lower quartile, and single-threaded stress-ng metrics reaching mid-tier levels. Large-block memory transfers achieve 73.07 GB/sec read and 35.12 GB/sec write bandwidth, supporting mid-tier PassMark database operations of 2,615.53. Designed for storage-intensive workloads requiring dedicated local drives, is4gen.xlarge delivers cost-efficient storage density without over-provisioning compute capacity, making it a functional choice for log aggregation, distributed file systems, intermediate analytics processing, and local caching databases.
